title: (fix) EventStreamRuntime: fix config passing on init (fixes test_runtime.py errors)
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

- `EventStreamRuntime` in its initialization did not copy over the passed `config` values to its own `self.config`, thus the base runtime did not get e.g. a changed value like `run_as_devin` as it happens in `test_runtime.py` (see: `test_ipython_multi_user`).
- Added more logging to runtime
- Changed max retry wait from 600 to 60 seconds as it otherwise would wait a painfully long time

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

In `test_runtime.py` several tests will be called twice for `run_as_devin` of True and False (root).
Even though the` _load_runtime` fixture instantiates a new `EventStreamRuntime` each time, the underlying base `Runtime` is only instantiated once and thus kept the same config values after the first instantiation.

Example: if test `test_ipython_multi_user` was first called with `run_as_devin` being True, the second run with fixture value of False would still cause the command in the container to be run with `opendevin` instead of `root`.

title: [Arch, Eval] Allowing injecting additional dependency to OD runtime docker image
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

Part of #2404, #3230.

For some evaluation (e.g., Logical reasoning, MINT) to work, you have to pre-install dependencies on the "OD's Python interpreter," which is used to power the "IPython."

We allow each eval to use their own `Dockerfile`, so the dependencies can be pre-installed for "bash", but not "IPython," since that's built on top of the user-provided base image on the fly:

https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/5469f67cb9a1f1b345dc872a1cdb799451fe5e27/evaluation/logic_reasoning/Dockerfile#L1-L5

title: [Arch] Use hash to avoid repeat building `EventStreamRuntime` image
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

Currently, when `sandbox.update_source_code = True` or env var `SANDBOX_UPDATE_SOURCE_CODE=True` is set, OpenDevin will *always* re-build an `od_runtime_dev` docker images (see https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/main/opendevin/runtime/client/README.md for more explanation). 

https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/blob/abec52abfe45333d127c023b71b65e3309e35c7b/opendevin/runtime/utils/runtime_build.py#L238-L246

However, there are cases when the "source code" and "Dockerfile" for the build are unchanged across different runs (e.g., running SWE-Bench evaluation twice on the same code base), which creates unnecessary rebuild that wastes compute and storage.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- This PR uses `dirhash` to calculate the hash based on the content and file structure of the docker build folder and uses it to tag `od_runtime_dev` images. This allows the unchanged docker build folder (source code and Dockerfile) to reuse existing images.


---

title: [Arch] Streamline EventStream Runtime Image Building Logic
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

The previous logic of runtime build is complex to wrap one's head around (e.g., if you don't set `update_source_code=True` while developing, you might be scratching your head wondering what's going on, and it turns out you used an outdated image).

Furthermore, the `update_source_code=True` is always set in most `evaluation/` (#3230) to ensure that the evaluation always reflects the current code. In #3243, we try to use directory hash to track the source code and `Dockerfile` used to build each sandbox image and hopefully avoid repeat rebuilding for evaluation.

However, I found the existing logic still requires an additional round of re-build for evaluation instances if `update_source_code=True`:
1. The first time running of SWE-Bench instance docker image "AAA:T" with source code hash ("abc") will build "od_runtime:AAA_tag_T", which is also tagged to "od_runtime:abc"
2. Assume the source code is unchanged, the second time running of SWE-Bench instance, it will detect "od_runtime:AAA_tag_T" exists, and since `update_source_code=True`, it will skip checking the hash, and rebuild an "od_runtime_dev:AAA_tag_T".

After drinking a bit, carefully maintaining my BAC level, and reaching the Ballmer's Peak, I realized the `update_source_code` might not be necessary at all.

![](https://imgs.xkcd.com/comics/ballmer_peak.png)


---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR removes `update_source_code`, and re-write the logic to keep track of runtime images:

Given a user-specified arbitrary docker image (e.g., `ubuntu:22.04`), it will be converted to an OpenDevin-supported Docker image.

The resulting image will be tagged as both:
- `{target_image_repo}:{target_image_hash_tag}`
- `{target_image_repo}:{target_image_tag}`

Explanation:
- `target_image_hash_tag` is the hash of the docker build folder (containing source code and Dockerfile).
    And same hash means the image is built from scratch with the *exact SAME source code* on the
    exact Dockerfile (i.e., same base image name & version).
- `target_image_tag` is the generic tag for the target image that's generic and resembles the "latest" tag
    in the docker image naming convention for a particular {repo}:{tag} pair.
    For example, od_runtime:od_v0.8.3_ubuntu_tag_22.04 means the latest OpenDevin v0.8.3 image built from scratch on top of
    ubuntu:22.04.

How does the image building works:
1. We convert the base image (e.g., `ubuntu:22.04`) into od_runtime image name (e.g., `od_runtime:od_v0.8.3_ubuntu_tag_22.04`)
2. We create a docker build folder (assuming we build from scratch), generate Dockerfile and copy over source code, and calculate a hash `from_scratch_hash`.
3. If the image exists with the same hash (e.g., `od_runtime:{from_scratch_hash}`), we will not build any image, and will pull that image and use it as it.
4. If the exact hash is not found (e.g., `od_runtime:{from_scratch_hash}`), but a recent OD runtime of the same image exists (e.g., `od_runtime:od_v0.8.3_ubuntu_tag_22.04`), we will try to rebuild the new image (e.g., `od_runtime:{from_scratch_hash}`) based on the latest image (e.g., `od_runtime:od_v0.8.3_ubuntu_tag_22.04`) to save some dependency installation time.
6. If the image hash is not found (e.g., `od_runtime:{from_scratch_hash}`) AND we cannot re-use the latest relavant image (e.g., `od_runtime:od_v0.8.3_ubuntu_tag_22.04`), we will build it completely from scratch.

---
**Other references**

title: ci: try to fix runtime build when exact hash for runtime image is found
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

Issue: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/actions/runs/10276535264/job/28437269516
When `runtime_build.py` detects the current codebase has the exact same hash as an existing image, it will not produce `Dockerfile`, which causes the above workflow to fail to build the image.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- This PR adjusts the workflow to *skip* the workflow build process and download the exact match hash image for subsequent workflow.

---

title: Clear history at the beginning of a new task🧹
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**
Clearing history at the beginning of a new task ensures that any previous data or context is removed, reducing the risk of errors or confusion. This can enhance the accuracy and relevance of the task being performed, preventing any carryover from past tasks. This update addresses any open issues related to context management and data integrity.

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
The PR introduces a mechanism to clear the history at the start of each new task. This design decision is made to maintain a clean state and ensure that tasks are executed with a fresh context. This approach avoids potential conflicts and errors that may arise from residual data.

title: fix: workspace folder permission & app container cannot access client API
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

Requires #3299 and #3301 to be merge first.

**Issue 1: Workspace folder permission**

In #3282, I tried to fix the dubious ownership issue by "chown" the whole mounted folder to the current `user_id`, but it raised a new issue while I was trying to fix things in #3299: When I mount a folder own by "me" with group "staff", that "chmod" will fail, possibly due to MacOS's permission management.

On second thought, as long as the mounted workspace is owned by the current user "me" and the user id is set properly to the OpenDevin application, this permission issue / dubious ownership **should not** happen in the first place. I think the original issue probably arises when i try have the agent running as root and commit to my workspace (owned by "me").

**Issue 2: After build OpenDevin `app` docker application, the backend cannot access the runtime API**

Because It will try to access `localhost:{port}`, instead of `host.docker.internal:{port}`.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

**Fix issue 1**
- Remove extra git config setting (these are already done in "client.py")
- Only chown when `/workspace` does not exists (in the case of mounted workspace, we should assume `/workspace` is already there)
- Change the test case to do not use mounted folder: `pytest` will create tmp dir owned by root, while the UID we send to OpenDevin is actually the current user "me", which cause weird behavior of the test.
- Improve the logging, especially when we are waiting to connect to the API server inside a docker container. Before this change, it will hang for a long time without giving any log / errors.

**Fix issue 2**
- Add "api_hostname" to config, and set it to "host.docker.internal" in `app` docker

---
**Other references**

title: Bug fix drag resize
body:
The first time you mouse down to drag resize a panel it does not work. It only works on subsequent mouse down events.

The reason is that the current implementation has a flaw (It is not surprising as this is something difficult to get right)
`onMouseDown` calls `setDividerPosition` which triggers a re-render, making the code inside useEffect obsolete - it is applied to a context which no longer exists.

The update moves the onMouseMove and onMouseUp inside the useEffect and adds a destructor, meaning that:

* `onMouseMove` and `onMouseUp` are not applied and do not exist unless a mouse down has occurred, setting the `dividerPosition`
* `onMouseMove` resizes the ref but does not trigger a re-render.
* `onMouseUp` removes the event listeners and triggers a re-render
* The destructor (Called in the event of a re-render) removes the event listeners  anyway.

Thanks to @​brandonmcconnell, @​manavm1990, @​langy, @​jamesreaco and @​jamaluddinrumi for sponsoring tailwind-merge! ❤️

v2.5.0

New Features

  • Performance improvements in mergeClassList by @​XantreDev in dcastil/tailwind-merge#450 and @​rortan134 in dcastil/tailwind-merge#445
  • Use arrow functions where possible to help with minification by @​VIKTORVAV99 in dcastil/tailwind-merge#449

Bug Fixes

  • Fix bg-opacity arbitrary percentages not being recognized properly by @​dcastil in dcastil/tailwind-merge#451

Full Changelog: https://github.com/dcastil/tailwind-merge/compare/v2.4.0...v2.5.0

title: Feat:  unsaved file content
body:
### Before Changes

When you make changes in the code editor, if you click into a different file, the changes are lost.
e.g.:
I write some changes:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da75b54e-84d1-484a-846b-65317f9e9d14)

But if I click into a different file, they are lost! (There is no dialog or warning to prevent this!)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccd9b5ec-5f8a-407f-b896-d8fac640a6f4)

### After Changes

We store changes even after you click out of a file. Files with unsaved changes are marked with a "*", and a cancel button was added to clear changes. (My original idea was to use local storage / indexed db to store changes, but I have not implemented this for this iteration - so a page refresh will still clear edits)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62ad3dc5-5ebf-4066-b1b5-9001506842bb)

I can click to a different file and make changes there too:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e90247cc-97c8-4bbf-8bb1-ee2fb03e380d)

Clicking back to the original displays the unsaved changes:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fecd242c-fb9d-4aa5-89da-7d3909870917)

Changes are only saved / cancelled when the page is refreshed or the button is clicked.

### Under the hood

I added an array of fileStates to the redux state - this allows for determining whether there is unsavedContent, and displaying different UI states in the file explorer

### Open Questions

I think some UI review is in order - making sure this is consistent with where we want the product to go, and that this UI is intuitive.

title: Group docusaurus dependabot updates
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

Docusaurus requires multiple packages be upgraded at the same time, causing dependabot updates to fail:
- https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/3347
- https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/3345
- https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/3343

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR uses [dependabot groups](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-version-updates/configuration-options-for-the-dependabot.yml-file#groups) to group these into a single PR, which should hopefully solve the problem.

body:

title: (fix) exclude Python cache files/folders from sdist
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

Fixes #3169 to avoid permission errors upon call of `build` (sdist)

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Added special manifest file to exclude Python cache files and folders from sdist.
These cache files are not needed, but can cause errors at runtime due to different file permissions.

title: Handle error observations in codeact
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

This PR fixes https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/3356 , which was causing CodeAct to die on an `ErrorObservation`, because no message was being produced for this.

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR makes sure that:
- Adds a message for CodeAct so that it creates a message for ErrorObservation
- Makes it so that a `ValueError` is raised on an unhandled observation in CodeAct, because all observations should be handled
- Adds tests for CodeAct's get message function
- Adds some documentation for AgentDelegateAction, where the arguments were unclear

The `_init_user` method now first checks, if the given username (e.g. `opendevin`) already exists.
If yes, it can return early.

Otherwise it'll try to add the user with the given user id (usually 1000) and **IF** that fails with a `not unique` error, it will increase the user id and retry, e.g.
```py
04:57:04 - opendevin:WARNING: client.py:158 - UID 1000 is not unique. Incrementing UID and retrying...
04:57:04 - opendevin:DEBUG: client.py:153 - Added user opendevin successfully with UID 1001. Output: []
```

Only under rare circumstances this should cause issues, but happy to refine it further in followup PR.

title: feat: support remote runtime
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

This is required for the hosted version of OpenHands.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

* This PR adds a "RemoteRuntime" that connects the OpenHands backend to a remote runtime API that has feature parity with local docker EventStream runtime.
* It has been locally tested and passed all the test runtime tests. Way to run: `SANDBOX_API_KEY="DM ME FOR THE KEY" TEST_RUNTIME=remote pytest -n 16 -vvxss tests/runtime`
* Support running tests in parallel - because we can run these runtime in parallel (the good thing about cloud!)

---
**Other references**
author: xingyaoww

title: Fix restore cli sessions
body:
There are no issues posted, but this is a fix for a real issue: cannot restore history from the event stream if running headless.

This PR proposes a fix that keeps it simple but is starting to introduce a bit of flexibility in handling command-line sessions:
- a command line arg "-n" or "--name" for the session name
- start using jwt_secret for the sid.

Maybe sometime we'll want a real cli client, this is just a bit on the road. 😄 

Note: this only concerns the sid that is used as name for the event stream. All uses of `create_runtime` in evals create their own `sid` too and send it, so we fix the uniqueness of their respective event stream from there. This PR doesn't change that for the container name there is more unique stuff added.
author: enyst

title: Fix: Bump max_iterations when resuming due to throttling
body:
This is intended to address https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/3323

There was a bug where when you reached the `max_iterations`, the UI would keep asking you to resume after every single request. This resets the iteration count. (100 by default - so you get 100 more requests before the session pauses again)

## Testing
I didn't want to make 100 requests each time, so I temporarily updated the `max_iterations` in my local config.toml from 100 to 2. ;)

## Sample Output
I asked the agent to write a couple of poems - it now resets the iteration count when resuming, so that you can hit `max_iterations` (In my case 3) before the agent stops again:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f1d690b-0990-463e-8a88-4d5c83a4f123)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ade300e0-b13c-43c0-b2db-15f7fc5dd421)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77c938a3-76f4-4958-84f2-c169050ea7ab)
author: tofarr

title: Add prompt caching (Sonnet, Haiku only)
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**
Add prompt caching to codeact agent and log token cached. 


---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/3397

1. Adds the cache_prompt: bool parameter to the Message class.
2. The Codeact agent checks if the model supports caching by using the supports_caching_prompt attributed created in the llm class.
3. Added cache breakpoints to the system prompt, example, and the last two user messages.
4. Moved the reminder to a new message, appended at the end, rather than appending it to the last message (which was preventing the last message from being cached).
5. Added logs for cached tokens at the end of the response log file.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e20a6c1-4f5b-4765-b576-4cd33224e6b4




It doesn't seem like Gemini caching support has been added to litellm, so only added support for claude for now. https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/4284

---
**Other references**
author: Kaushikdkrikhanu

title: Logging fixes and improvements
body:
This PR proposes a few fixes and improvements to logging:

- [x] clean up ANSI characters from the file logs
- [x] for restored sessions, keep new logs in the same place
- [x] fix useless dir creation in some cases
- [x] refactor older logging to f-strings (initially all calls used old-style %s). There might be some performance cost, but we're using f-strings for a long time anyway, and I'd suggest we can deal with it if or when it happens.
author: enyst

title: Use generic types
body:
Since we support python 3.11+, we use generic types (list, tuple) and simpler syntax (| None). But Copilot likes the old capitalized versions from the typing module (List, Tuple), and they sneak in the codebase, so it seems that once in a while we need to clear them out.

For example, older clearing: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/1680

body: Our config silently ignores unknown keys in the config.toml on startup: https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/3074 This PR prints a warning if a key is not found # Background Standard python dataclasses throw an error if you try to use an attribute that does not exist. title: (fix) jobs need if condition modified to enable run on PR push
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

`if` condition for `ghcr_push` and other jobs needed extra checks to not be skipped on PR merge.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

The `if` condition for this job states that it should only run when:
- The GitHub reference is refs/heads/main (i.e., pushes to the main branch)
- OR when the reference starts with refs/tags/ (i.e., when a new tag is created)

When a **_pull request_** is merged to the main branch, the workflow runs in the context of the pull request, not the main branch itself.

In a pull request context, the github.ref would typically be something like refs/pull/123/merge, not refs/heads/main. 

This means the condition github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' evaluates to false.

To fix this and ensure the ghcr_push job runs when a PR is merged to main, the condition should be modified to include pull request merges.

(Fix provided by Sonnet)

---

title: Add credits and licenses for code from other projects
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces?**

The intention of this PR is to add a place (Credits.md) where we can references external projects whose code we include, adapt, or copy directly. For example, we copy and/or adapt:
- SWE Agent code, Aider linting code, BrowserGym's demo agent
- reference implementations for eval benchmarks like AgentBench, etc.

Example that this PR aims to fix (or to offer a way to fix): in agentskills/aider we have the full text of the Apache License. It's there because it's with code adapted from Aider. That's okay, but this approach doesn't really scale as we may add more, e.g. can't keep adding full texts of AL 2.0 again in other directories, and moreover, as we refactor agent skills or further modify things, code may move around.

The way this PR proposes we can do this:
- have readme/comments to refer in the code to their source projects (and for AL 2.0 what modifications were made), like many localized readme we have already
- list the projects and their licenses in the Credits.md file
- include full text of all licenses in the Credits.md file.

Please note:
- I reviewed the licensing of the benchmark reference implementations (code), however this review did not include datasets. We may want to do that too sometime...
- One of the repos in evaluation has a license that is not Open Source, it has restrictions on ML. https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/pull/3436/files#diff-7ddc0d1fb1cd484a1b4abfe10b5bd46a7d455c6ecf8e3228ebb4f19029bf389cR275

We may want to give it some thought. It's not a very restrictive license, but I think people should be able to trust that this repo can be used as everyone knows permissive licenses always allow, and that is not exactly the case. @neubig

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
https://github.com/OpenDevin/OpenDevin/issues/3397
1. Detects Anthropic model and caches the latest prompts (greater than 1024 tokens). 
2. Processes prompts to other models separately
Anthropic does not allow caching of message history shorter than 1024 tokens, but instead of throwing a BadRequestError if cache-control is used for the message, it now processes shorter messages without caching them. Thus, caching can be on by default.
Can add other models as they allow caching.

0.6.1

Release Notes

This is a hotfix release to address an issue with ruff-pre-commit. In v0.6, Ruff changed its behavior to lint and format Jupyter notebooks by default; however, due to an oversight, these files were still excluded by default if Ruff was run via pre-commit, leading to inconsistent behavior. body:
Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 1.26.4 to 2.1.0.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

2.1.0 (Aug 18, 2024)

NumPy 2.1.0 Release Notes

NumPy 2.1.0 provides support for the upcoming Python 3.13 release and drops support for Python 3.9. In addition to the usual bug fixes and updated Python support, it helps get us back into our usual release cycle after the extended development of 2.0. The highlights for this release are:

  • Support for the array-api 2023.12 standard.
  • Support for Python 3.13.
  • Preliminary support for free threaded Python 3.13.

Python versions 3.10-3.13 are supported in this release.

New functions

New function numpy.unstack

A new function np.unstack(array, axis=...) was added, which splits an array into a tuple of arrays along an axis. It serves as the inverse of [numpy.stack]{.title-ref}.

(gh-26579)

Deprecations

  • The fix_imports keyword argument in numpy.save is deprecated. Since NumPy 1.17, numpy.save uses a pickle protocol that no longer supports Python 2, and ignored fix_imports keyword. This keyword is kept only for backward compatibility. It is now deprecated.

    (gh-26452)

  • Passing non-integer inputs as the first argument of [bincount]{.title-ref} is now deprecated, because such inputs are silently cast to integers with no warning about loss of precision.

    (gh-27076)

Expired deprecations

  • Scalars and 0D arrays are disallowed for numpy.nonzero and numpy.ndarray.nonzero.

    (gh-26268)

  • set_string_function internal function was removed and PyArray_SetStringFunction was stubbed out.

Does it fix any open issues?** The models input dumps all the raw LiteLLM IDs that cause slight performance issues and overwhelm the user with options. --- **Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions** ### Default behaviour This PR breaks down the input into a Provider input and Models input. Given the provider, a filtered models list will be available for the user to choose. - Changed default `LLM_MODEL` to `openai/gpt-4o` from `gpt-4o` The user can see the "Verified" providers and models that we recommend and know work well with OpenHands. `utils/verified-models.ts` ```ts export const VERIFIED_PROVIDERS = ["openai", "azure", "anthropic"]; export const VERIFIED_MODELS = ["gpt-4o", "claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0"]; ``` If preferred, the user can set a custom LLM model. - New settings were added, `CUSTOM_LLM_MODEL` and `USING_CUSTOM_LLM`. That way, the socket class sends the appropriate LLM with the `LLM_MODEL` key if `settings.USING_CUSTOM_LLM` is `true`. ### Tests - ~85 - 90%+ test coverage ### Notes - Need to confirm which are the verified providers and models we want to set and display to the user. - Need to confirm that the new way of setting custom LLM models is OK - Since LiteLLM does not maintain consistency between supported models (some are not returned at all and just say they support it by append `some-provider/`), most are dumped in an `other` provider. Need to confirm if it is OK, which ones do we want to "pull out", and if there are alternative ways to handle this (TBH considering going to the LiteLLM repo and making the changes for consistency myself) **TODO** - [x] Add a switch to allow the user to switch between LiteLLM models and a custom model - [ ] ~~Investigate providers that offer custom models~~ - [x] Input validation - [x] Set verified models and providers - [x] Bug fixes **Accidentally removed #3514 after re-forking**

This PR updates feedbackmodal to fix two things:
1. It fixes the link from `share-openhands` to `share` as that's the link on the new version of the All Hands AI web site.
2. It removes the password from the link. The password should be kept private, and if the password is included in the link, people might accidentally share it with others.

title: Add back docker caching, simplify docker builds
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

[This PR](https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/pull/2456) made a bunch of changes to the image workflow. Some of the changes are great, but we lost a few things as well:
* we stopped pushing image tags for PRs (which is helpful for QA)
* we lost caching
* multi-arch became part of a matrix, leading (I think) to longer build times


---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

* Changes `build.sh` to build a single multi-arch image, rather than iterating through each platform
* Adds back the `--push` option to the build script
* Removes the `.tar` image files and artifacts, as well as a lot of plumbing for those images and tag names

This is intended to address https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/3527

As pointed out by a user, our build on pypi does not include agenthub. The package on pypi is pretty much broken due to missing files and dependencies.

title: (discarded) Improve CodeActAgent's file editing reliability
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

A recurring issue for `CodeActAgent` and models like Sonnet is the plain removal of content and ignoring the fact, that `open_file` only shows a limited number of lines. The latter often results in Sonnet to just _assume_ that it did read the _full_ file, then edits with improper content and potentially corrupting the file (especially when > 100 lines).

Wording changes for
- `open_file`:  with regard to amount of displayed lines; written out method names for `scroll_up` / `scroll_down`
- `edit_file_by_replace`: mention this is for existing files and `to_replace` must be non-empty
- `system_prompt.j2` template: added several specific file-related operation hints

**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

If a folder in the workspace is being removed (in the actual filesystem, outside of OpenHands) and then in the UI the "Refresh" icon on the file explorer is clicked, an error "500 internal server error" will appear in the UI. This PR prevents this.

title: (fix) Enable and log if logging to file is enabled
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

PR #3429 basically disabled any logging to file by introducing a new env-only flag `LOG_TO_FILE` which is not documented and not part of the config (`config.toml` file). And if enabled, there was no indication where these logs were written.
If run from source (make build/run), these logs are no longer available "locally", but only inside the runtime container!

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR changes 2 things:
- enable logging to file also if only DEBUG is active
- output a logging message to backend terminal like below:
```sh
    |12:37:46 - openhands:DEBUG: logger.py:178 - Logging initialized
    |12:37:46 - openhands:INFO: logger.py:181 - Logging to file is enabled. Logging to /openhands/code/logs
```

title: New README for OpenHands/openhands/runtime folder
body:
**What is the problem that this fixes or functionality that this introduces? Does it fix any open issues?**

OpenHands - given a 10-step plan - generated a README.md for the `runtime` folder.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

1. My first prompt was to generate a plan:
```
Review below task and create a plan with detailed steps on what should be done:
This is a documentation task:
- enter folder /workspace/OpenHands/openhands/runtime
- this folder contains mainly backend files, some are only for execution in a docker sandbox
- write your findings into README.md in markdown syntax
- try to create detailed, text-only workflow from the python files in runtime.py as well as the sub-folders client
- for further analysis feel free to review other python files and folders in the /workspace/OpenHands/openhands/ folder
```

2. The resulting plan I saved locally into a file `task-plan.md`:
```md
# Documentation Task Plan for OpenHands Runtime Folder

1. Navigate to the target directory:
   - Change directory to /workspace/OpenHands/openhands/runtime

2. List and analyze the contents of the runtime folder:
   - Identify Python files, especially runtime.py
   - Note any subdirectories, particularly the client folder

3. Analyze runtime.py:
   - Read the file contents
   - Identify all public functions, classes, and their purposes
   - Note any important imports or dependencies
   - Understand the overall workflow and structure

4. Examine the client subfolder:
   - List and analyze Python files in the client folder
   - Identify the purpose of each file
   - Note all classes, all their public functions, or workflows

5. Create a detailed workflow description:
   - Combine insights from runtime.py and client folder analysis
   - Create a step-by-step, text-only workflow description
   - Focus on the main processes and their interactions

6. Prepare the README.md file:
   - Create a new README.md file if it doesn't exist
   - Use proper Markdown syntax for formatting
   - Structure the document with clear headings and sections

7. Write the documentation in README.md:
   - Introduction to the runtime folder and its purpose
   - Overview of the main components (runtime.py and client folder)
   - Detailed workflow description
   - Any important notes about Docker sandbox execution
   - Mention of related files or dependencies in the parent directory

8. Review and refine the documentation:
   - Ensure clarity and completeness of the workflow description
   - Check Markdown formatting
   - Proofread for any errors or inconsistencies

9. Finalize the README.md file:
    - Make sure all relevant information is included
    - Ensure the document is well-structured and easy to read

10. Repeat steps 2 to 8 for folder /workspace/OpenHands/openhands/server/session
and the /workspace/OpenHands/openhands/server/listen.py file and append your
findings to the first mentioned README.md file.
```

3. My next prompt was a simple prompt to have it implement it:

```md
Implement the plan as written in task-plan.md
```

4. The resulting file is this PR's `README.md`

The server-related parts of the generated readme were then moved to the existing README.md in the server folder.

title: chore(deps-dev): bump jsdom from 24.1.1 to 25.0.0 in /frontend
body:
Bumps [jsdom](https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom) from 24.1.1 to 25.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from jsdom's releases.

Version 25.0.0

This major release changes the prototype of a jsdom's EventTarget.prototype to point to the Object.prototype inside the jsdom, instead of pointing to the Node.js Object.prototype. Thus, the prototype chain of Window stays entirely within the jsdom, never crossing over into the Node.js realm.

This only occurs when runScripts is set to non-default values of "dangerously" or "outside-only", as with the default value, there is no separate Object.prototype inside the jsdom.

This will likely not impact many programs, but could cause some changes in instanceof behavior, and so out of an abundance of caution, we're releasing it as a new major version.

Version 24.1.3

  • Fixed calls to postMessage() that were done as a bare property (i.e., postMessage() instead of window.postMessage()).

Version 24.1.2

  • Fixed an issue with the in operator applied to EventTarget methods, e.g. 'addEventListener' in window, which only appeared in Node.js ≥22.5.0. (legendecas)
  • Fixed the events fired by blur(): it no longer fires focus and focusin on the Document, and blur and focusout no longer have their relatedTarget property set. (asamuzaK)

This will likely not impact many programs, but could cause some changes in instanceof behavior, and so out of an abundance of caution, we're releasing it as a new major version.

title: (enh) Improve CodeActAgent's file editing reliability
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Improve system prompt to reduce file editing errors made by LLM.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

A recurring issue with the agent skills for file editing and models like Sonnet were incorrect calls of methods, that caused extra steps for the LLM to get it right.

Issues like:
- First attempt to create a new file was followed by a replace command with empty content, which we do not allow. Causing multiple, preventable steps and costs.
- An `open_file` only shows a limited number of lines and it is apparently _really hard_ to convince an LLM to read a file fully in order to analyze it. This often resulted in Sonnet to just _assume_ to know a file content from just the initial 100 lines.
Subsequent edits of it to the same file then resulted in replacement not found (no edit action performed -> edit loop), or the file content becoming incomplete and/or syntactically wrong.

Changes (in short):
- The system prompt (`system_prompt.j2`) text and file ops docstrings got applied several tweaks with concrete hints.
- `file_ops.py`: in order to reduce noise in the logs, errors are mostly output as plain text to the LLM and no longer by raising an exception (avoiding lengthy tracebacks)
- Unit tests adopted accordingly
- Integration tests: removed references to server runtime (incl. mock .log files) and TEST_RUNTIME

**TODO:**
- [X] Units tests are working
- [x] Integration tests need regeneration
- [ ] SWE bench eval

---
This is a rebased PR version of #3550 but now on repo branch, so other maintainers can edit.

title: (feat) runtime: in _wait_until_alive upon start wait for client to have initialized too
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

EventStreamRuntime will wait for runtime client to be initialized once, for up to 10s. 

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

The runtime starts the client and should wait for its full initialization before resuming normal processing.
This will only be done once and only for up to 10 seconds so to not get stuck.

@xingyaoww Let me know what you think about this approach.

body:

This PR introduces tools to enhance context gathering and improve the localization of specific files, classes, functions, or variable declarations critical for resolving issues. The PR integrates modules from [OpenAutoCoder Agentless](https://github.com/OpenAutoCoder/Agentless) and [RepoGraph](https://github.com/ozyyshr/RepoGraph) to further aid in the localization of code relevant to the issue.

title: Fix security analyzer
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

This PR simplifies the interface to SecurityAnalyzer so that it is clear from calling code that the security analyzer is subscribing to the event stream.

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Changes the interface from

```python
    event_stream = EventStream('main', file_store)
    InvariantAnalyzer(event_stream)
```

to

```python
    event_stream = EventStream('main', file_store)
    security_analyzer = InvariantAnalyzer()
    event_stream.subscribe(
        EventStreamSubscriber.SECURITY_ANALYZER, security_analyzer.on_event
    )
```

This PR also changes `on_event()` to also take the `EventStream` as an argument, as it is used by `InvariantAnalyzer`.


**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

Fixes #3624

title: (enh) Aider-Bench: make resumable with skip_num arg
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Make Aider-Bench run resumable with optional `SKIP_NUM` env flag

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- added optional `SKIP_NUM` env flag (int) which specifies the number of instances in the dataset to be skipped first, thus offering to resume a bench
- in `shared.py`, the `prepare_dataset` got a new optional parameter
- in that method, if a `skip_num` was given, it will combine this with the `eval_n_limit` number, so a run could skip the first 42 incidents and then run 10 instances
- temporarily changed links for huggingface evaluations to use the old repo name as the new one while the new one is in the works
author: tobitege

title: (enh) StuckDetector: fix+enhance syntax error loop detection
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Loop detection of one type of syntax error was broken. Expanded to 4 types of syntax errors.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

There was only one type of syntax error in the stuck detection, like `unterminated string literal`.
However, this was broken as the detection only checked a limited range of characters for it.

Instead, the detection is now expanded to the last 4 lines of the observation.
In recent enhancements there were potentially 2 lines added for interpreter and prompt,
making the check basically skip the detection each time.

Unit tests adapted and fixed accordingly.

List of detected errors is now this:
```py
    SYNTAX_ERROR_MESSAGES = [
        'SyntaxError: unterminated string literal (detected at line',
        'SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?',
        'SyntaxError: incomplete input',
        "E999 SyntaxError: unmatched ')'",
    ]
```

The added errors is a distinct collection from 98 occurences in a bench that I ran.

Sourced from tree-sitter's releases.

v0.23.0

Additions:

  • Node.child_containing_descendant(descendant)
  • Tree.language (getter)
  • Query.pattern_count (getter)
  • Query.capture_count (getter)
  • Query.match_limit (getter)
  • Query.did_exceed_match_limit (getter)
  • Query.set_match_limit(match_limit): returns self
  • Query.set_max_start_depth(max_start_depth): returns self
  • Query.set_byte_range(byte_range): returns self
  • Query.set_point_range(point_range): returns self
  • Query.disable_pattern(index): returns self
  • Query.disable_capture(capture): returns self
  • Query.pattern_settings(index)
  • Query.pattern_assertions(index)
  • Query.start_byte_for_pattern(index)
  • Query.end_byte_for_pattern(index)
  • Query.is_pattern_rooted(index)
  • Query.is_pattern_non_local(index)
  • Query.is_pattern_guaranteed_at_step(offset)
  • QueryError (exception class)
  • QueryPredicate (typing protocol)

Removals:

  • Parser.set_language(language)
  • Parser.set_included_ranges(ranges)
  • Parser.set_timeout_micros(timeout)
  • Node.sexp()
  • Tree.text()
  • TreeCursor.goto_first_child_for_point(row, column)
  • LookaheadIterator.reset(language, state)

Changes:

  • Language() accepts a capsule as an argument.
  • Parser.parse(...) no longer accepts a keep_text argument.
  • Query.captures(...)
    • Range arguments were removed (use set_* instead).
    • Added an argument for custom query predicates.
    • Return type was changed to dict[str, list[Node]].
  • Query.matches(...)
    • Range arguments were removed (use set_* instead).
    • Added an argument for custom query predicates.
    • Return type was changed to list[tuple[int, dict[str, list[Node]]]].
  • TreeCursor.goto_first_child_for_byte(byte) returns int | None.
  • TreeCursor.goto_first_child_for_point(point) returns int | None.

title: Edit linting: use line mapping to rule out irrelevant errors
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Please read #3412 for more detail. To simply put, previous work uses the diff of linting error messages from pre-edit-lint and post-edit-lint to rule out "irrelevant" linting errors. The biggest flaw is that error messages could be generic - leading to both false positives and false negatives. This PR uses a more robust approach: line numbers.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Before edit, we run linting once, and record the error messages from the linter. After edit, we run linting once again, and also record the error messages. We then compare the line numbers from both pre-edit-lint and post-edit-lint. We rule out errors that are irrelevant to the edit (i.e. we remove errors that exist in both pre-edit-lint and post-edit-lint). This is non-trivial because line numbers might change. Luckily, since we only allow edits at a single place at a time, it is not too hard to figure out line mapping.

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

#3412

title: (fix) CodeActAgent: fix issues with vision support in prompts
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Fixes #2848  - fix wrong `content` format sent to LLM's that do not support structured messages (related to vision/caching).
Should also fix #3408 

---

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Since the introduction of image support, the messages to the LLM have as `content` an additional data structure level, that causes errors on different LLM/providers (Gemini on OpenRouter; Llama 3.1 on Groq).

Example error that occured on e.g. Groq API with lama 3.1-70B (line breaks added for readability):
```
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': "'messages.0' : 
for 'role:system' the following must be satisfied[('messages.0.content' : value must be a string)]", 
'type': 'invalid_request_error'}}
```

This PR now sends `content` again as a single text if `supports_prompt_caching` is not active.
Error messages during completion showed up as "BadRequestError" or "OpenAIError".

- added option to explicitly disable vision support (in case admin wants to save costs)
- added LLM method `vision_is_active`, which takes into account whether the model actually supports images (as reported by litellm) and the option to disable it
- Class `Message`, new method `format_messages`: processing of llm messages dependent on flag (vision active or not), i.e. return with "flat" `text` attribute as this is for litellm, not a specific provider
- Moved appliance of `extra_headers` for prompt caching out of `CodeActAgent` directly into LLM's completion, so that it will be active for all agents
- Updates to regenerate workflow yaml to enforce regeneration and fix python version; added several optional parameters as inputs when run
- Several tweaks to integration tests' processing files
  - Raised `MAX_ITERATIONS` from 15 to 20 as some (successful) tests need more steps now with Sonnet
  - `WORKSPACE_MOUNT_PATH` got wrong default assigned (pwd), which - _I think_ - was the cause for several file-related tests where files were read and written in totally different folders, which no longer occur (in WSL)
  - Commented out `test_ipython_module` integration test: it is no longer deterministic with e.g. Sonnet, as there are more than expected/configured steps now!
  - Terminal output tweaked (e.g. less empty lines)
  - `Step 4`: added an extra "cd" command to prevent "No such file or directory"
  - `test_browse_internet`: this has been a thorn in my WSL-side for long time. In `regenerate.sh` moved the test http server calls into the main loop or the whole process wouldn't work (either it was a different agent or a different run), relying on the external script. The previously used  fixture in `conftest.py` only caused connection errors (at least WSL).
- Updated several CodeActAgent/CodeActSWEAgent integration mock files due to prompt/agent skills changes
- In client runtime explicitly reraise a `ConnectionRefusedError` (e.g. docker erroring about ports already in use) as this otherwise would never  come back. well, like in an hour maybe...
- Fixed a frequent exception in `file_ops` when trying to a temp file to target folder, which in WSL caused a "cross device operation" error, which then not only prevented linting steps, but also frequently messed up integration test mock files due to an error line, that wouldn't happen on CLI! temp file is now created in same folder, but with a strongly random name, as we should already have write permissions in that folder anyways.
- Adapted a couple of unit tests to work with above changes

- [X] Integration tests fixed

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- Any colon `:` in a model name, like `nousresearch/hermes-3-llama-3.1-405b:extended` prevents logging to file as there won't be a folder created.
- If the use of the unit test is enabled (env var option), the LLM's have all different ideas on _how_ to _execute_ that test, which often resulted in timeouts. The instruction to the LLM has been improved to use the same format as the bench would use itself,
e.g. `python -m unittest {instance.instance_name}_test.py`

title: file_ops: Use tmp file for original linting
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Fix a potential issue that might lead to file corruption when edit linting is enabled

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

#3124 introduces a feature for editing: running linter twice before and after the change and only extract new errors introduced by the agent. This has some potential issues and I am working on #3649 to address them, but I feel like I am not gonna finish it in the next few days, and that PR has become harder and harder to review, thus this PR, which only focuses on a small improvement.

So what's the issue? When we run linters on the original file before our edits, we need to copy the original file and use a temporary file to lint, because *linting* may have side-effect (e.g. modifying the file in-place). I used the word "may" because:
1) Flake8 has no side-effect, so not a problem as of now.
2) We don't enforce this or document this "no side-effect" as a requirement for linter implementation, so side-effect is allowed.


Regardless, the "after-edit-linting" uses the same approach: backup the file before linting to avoid data corruption. We should keep our "before-edit-linting" consistent.

Why no new unittest that reproduces the issue? Well, as I have mentioned earlier, flake8 has no side-effect, so technically it's not a bug but a flaw. Therefore, there's no way to write a test that reproduces the issue.

title: Add documentation for CLI mode
body:
Fixes #3703

Add documentation for CLI mode in OpenHands.

* **New Documentation**: Add `docs/modules/usage/how-to/cli-mode.md` to document CLI mode.
  - Include instructions on starting an interactive OpenHands session via the command line.
  - Explain the difference between CLI mode and headless mode.
  - Provide examples of CLI commands and expected outputs.
* **Update Existing Documentation**: Modify `docs/modules/usage/how-to/headless-mode.md`.
  - Clarify the difference between headless mode and CLI mode.
  - Add a reference to the new CLI mode documentation.

body:
Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 1.26.4 to 2.1.1.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

2.1.0 (Aug 18, 2024)

NumPy 2.1.0 Release Notes

NumPy 2.1.0 provides support for the upcoming Python 3.13 release and drops support for Python 3.9. In addition to the usual bug fixes and updated Python support, it helps get us back into our usual release cycle after the extended development of 2.0. The highlights for this release are:

  • Support for the array-api 2023.12 standard.
  • Support for Python 3.13.
  • Preliminary support for free threaded Python 3.13.

Python versions 3.10-3.13 are supported in this release.

New functions

New function numpy.unstack

A new function np.unstack(array, axis=...) was added, which splits an array into a tuple of arrays along an axis. It serves as the inverse of [numpy.stack]{.title-ref}.

(gh-26579)

Deprecations

  • The fix_imports keyword argument in numpy.save is deprecated. Since NumPy 1.17, numpy.save uses a pickle protocol that no longer supports Python 2, and ignored fix_imports keyword. This keyword is kept only for backward compatibility. It is now deprecated.

    (gh-26452)

  • Passing non-integer inputs as the first argument of [bincount]{.title-ref} is now deprecated, because such inputs are silently cast to integers with no warning about loss of precision.

    (gh-27076)

Expired deprecations

  • Scalars and 0D arrays are disallowed for numpy.nonzero and numpy.ndarray.nonzero.

    (gh-26268)

  • set_string_function internal function was removed and PyArray_SetStringFunction was stubbed out.

title: hotfix: Anthropic provider points to the correct LiteLLM model ID
body:
**CHANGELOG**
- Selecting the anthropic provider now points to the correct litellm model

**PROBLEM**
LiteLLM returns two types of model IDs for Anthropic (and actually other providers too). The first type has a pattern as `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620`. The second is of the type `claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620` which is the one we want.

The first pattern is either outdated and incompatible and defaults/assumes a Bedrock configuration or the first pattern is actually for Bedrock configurations.

The helper functions that parse the models were using the first pattern and storing the second under the `other` provider.

**SOLUTION**
The parser now ignores the models with a `.` separator and groups the anthropic models with a `/` separator (e.g., `claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620` is now `anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620`).

Resolves #3708

title: (enh) CodeActAgent: improve message conversions and RateLimitErrors handling
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Improve rate limit error handling and logging; tweaked default `retry` values in case of LLM errors.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- urgent fix to `format_messages` in `Message` class that caused an empty message (and thus errors with LLM's).
- refactored a bit the tenacity `@retry` decorator to reduce duplicate code
- custom `wait` method for retry decorator to especially raise immediately the wait time for `RateLimitError` exceptions
- in case of an LLM error in CodeActAgent completion, log the error again to log and a shortened version to the UI as well
- `LLMConfig` class: changed default retry values to more sensible, lower values after testing to prevent ridiculously long wait times
- improved descriptions in the config template and docs

title: feat(workflow): Implement a simplified CoAct workflow
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

- This PR implements a simplified multi-agent workflow inspired by the [CoAct paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13381).
- Currently, in swe-bench eval, there are complex instances that OpenHands fails, especially ones that single `CodeActAgent` overlooks the buggy location. If we have a grounding test case for the issue, this workflow seems to help.
- An overkill-ish successful trajectory with replanning can be found [here](https://www.all-hands.dev/share?share_id=5d279ec840834fb326c8f3a2fcfc108bcbb27e4793c6a329e6515fa301c448ac).
- A task which `CoActPlannerAgent` finished but `CodeActAgent` failed (I expected both to be able to complete it):
  - [CoAct traj](https://www.all-hands.dev/share?share_id=197cb024a7eee24c8373b3ac1bbc5e905d274bbe0a869c3c4b7705158bcf4de6)
  - [CodeAct traj](https://www.all-hands.dev/share?share_id=6be13d7296b6bdfefdfc6e6a3a21e21198716a2ecd4494dd4962787f5105abe7)

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- Modify CodeAct to make it accept delegated task.
- Implement 2 new agents, planner and executor with the same abilities as CodeAct, different system prompts, additional action parsers.
- Nit: adjust the delegate message shown on UI.

---
Some next steps to improve this may be:
- [x] Try eval on some `swe-bench-lite` instances.
- [x] Adjust the system/user prompts and few-shot examples to further specialize the two agents. Also define the structure for the plan (e.g., its components, etc). 2 agents can now cooperate to finish a swe-bench issue.
- Use meta prompt to reinforce the actions of agents, to make sure it follows the workflow.
- Experiment with ability for the global planner to refuse the replan request from executor.
- Implement ability for the delegated agent (e.g., `BrowsingAgent` or `CoActExecutorAgent`) to persist its history through the multi-turn conversation.

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/3077

title: (enh) send status messages to UI during startup

**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Make it possible to send status messages from backend to UI.

---

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- Frontend: add status message display below existing agent status message area; additions to FE for a status message slice and handling
- The sent messages are actual translations keys as contained in `translation.json`, e.g. `STATUS$WAITING_FOR_CLIENT`
- Added loads of missing translations with the help of Sonnet
- In the `session.py` file, method `queue_status_message` is the main sender
- runtimes: added parameter to pass in a `status_message_callback` that is aimed
  to be called from inside the runtime if it wants to send status messages to the UI
- in `EventStreamRuntime` added only a couple status messages
- folder `server/session`: in `session.py` added a task to manage a status message queue which gets sent to the UI
- renamed `server/session/agent.py` to `agent_session.py` - too many files are just named `agent`, imho

---

**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

There are many open issues which stem from the fact, that during startup, there is no extra feedback.
Especially if no docker images are present a lot of time-consuming operations have to be taken care of at initial startup. This can take several minutes, only on repeat sesssions this time would be shorter (or a fixed image were specified).

title: Add Handling of Cache Prompt When Formatting Messages
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**
Implements correct application of cache control headers in message formatting based on the cache_prompt flag.

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
This PR addresses an issue where the cache control header was not being correctly applied when formatting messages. The changes include:

1. Modified the `format_messages` function to track the `cache_prompt` flag for each content item in a message.
2. Implemented logic to combine `cache_prompt` flags from multiple content items using the OR operator.
3. Added a condition to include the `cache_control` key with the value 'ephemeral' in the formatted message when `cache_prompt` is True.
4. Updated the handling of different message types (string, dict, Message object) to properly check and apply the `cache_prompt` flag.

These changes ensure that the cache control header is correctly applied based on the `cache_prompt` flag of the content items, improving the caching behavior of the system.

---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**
Fixes https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/3772: Incorrect application of cache control headers in message formatting
author: ColeMurray

title: Add Anthropic Models to Cache Prompt
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**
Adds support for Anthropic models with 'anthropic/' prefix in cache prompting.

---

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
This pull request addresses an issue where Anthropic models with the 'anthropic/' prefix were not being correctly identified for cache prompting support. The changes include:

1. Added two new entries to the `cache_prompting_supported_models` list:
   - 'anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620'
   - 'anthropic/claude-3-haiku-20240307'

2. Retained the existing entries without the 'anthropic/' prefix to maintain backwards compatibility:
   - 'claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620'
   - 'claude-3-haiku-20240307'

This change ensures that the cache prompting feature correctly supports Anthropic models regardless of whether they are referenced with or without the 'anthropic/' prefix. This dual-entry approach allows for flexibility in model naming conventions while maintaining support for existing configurations.

The decision to keep both prefixed and non-prefixed versions was made to:
1. Support users who may be using the models with the 'anthropic/' prefix in their configurations.
2. Maintain compatibility for users who are already using the non-prefixed versions.

---

**Link of any specific issues this addresses**
Fixes https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/3774: Incorrect identification of Anthropic models in prompt cache supported models
author: ColeMurray

title: Regression fixes: LLM logging; client readiness (EventStreamRuntime)
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Fix logging of LLM messages (if enabled) and client readiness detection in EventStreamRuntime

---

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- Unfortunately a recent PR of mine broke the logging of LLM messages to file, which caused integration test mock files to miss the user prompt for some agents+test combos.
  EDIT: ~~Newer PR's since then started to fail.~~ The regeneration of integration mock files for PR's was problematic.
- For the `EventStreamRuntime` the client readiness detection was moved to the actual `LogBuffer` class. In some situations, depending on timing, OH could've gotten stuck on getting docker container logs. This detection was added to prevent premature sending of commands before the client was fully initialized (a container is signaled as ready several seconds before that).
- Several integration test mock files were regenerated for this PR.

title: [Feat] Added FileEditAction to enable edits using diff format.
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**
We want to switch from our current agenskills style (similar to https://aider.chat/docs/benchmarks.html#diff-func) to Aider's diff block (https://aider.chat/docs/benchmarks.html#diff) and how that would improve the editing performance.


---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR adds a new EditAction, with logic to parse these output in diff format in the CodeActParser (translating the diff into EditAction).
The EditAction is then executed inside the runtime (for now, we simply parse the diff format into search and replace blocks and manually call the existing agentskills to perform the edit)

We use the <execute_edit> tags to enclose the diff format. For example,
```
<execute_edit>
demo.py
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    print("hello")
=======
    print("goodbye")
>>>>>>> REPLACE
</execute_edit>
```
---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**
#3650

title: (enh) add caching@v4 action in workflows
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Reduce workflow runtime by applying specific caching action. Also removed 2 image test from matrix.

---

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

As per recent discussion in Slack, we have Nikolaik as the main base image and now remove the extra 2 image testing rounds from the workflow to reduce used resources/test times.

- The existing python setup action didn't need caching, it runs only ~10 seconds anyways
- Added cache@v4 action for poetry dependencies, which results in a ~1.1 GB cache entry (vastly different from the one reported in the "setting up python" step!)
- Thus, as long as the `poetry.lock` doesn't change, this cache entry will be usable across several runners/PR's, afaik
- Build image: < 9 min - reduction by several minutes (in other PR's I saw 13+ minutes)
- `Runtime Integration Tests` unchanged ~ 11 min.  
- `Test Runtime` "vanilla" was ~35+ min.
  - `test_env_vars.py`: optimization by combining 3 tests in one -> time saving TBD
- this PR got to ~44 min. total time, where others were 50+ min.
- Fixed some conditions' syntax related to forks

If anyone sees an error in the above causality for the reduced runtime other than the cache action, please let me know.

---

**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

Updates `eslint-plugin-import` from 2.29.1 to 2.30.0
Release notes

Sourced from eslint-plugin-import's releases.

v2.30.0

Added

  • dynamic-import-chunkname: add allowEmpty option to allow empty leading comments (#2942, thanks [@​JiangWeixian])
  • dynamic-import-chunkname: Allow empty chunk name when webpackMode: 'eager' is set; add suggestions to remove name in eager mode (#3004, thanks [@​amsardesai])
  • [no-unused-modules]: Add ignoreUnusedTypeExports option (#3011, thanks [@​silverwind])
  • add support for Flat Config (#3018, thanks [@​michaelfaith])

Fixed

  • [no-extraneous-dependencies]: allow wrong path (#3012, thanks [@​chabb])
  • [no-cycle]: use scc algorithm to optimize (#2998, thanks [@​soryy708])

  • newline-after-import: fix considerComments option when require (#2952, thanks [@​developer-bandi])

  • [Refactor] ExportMap: make procedures static instead of monkeypatching exportmap (#2982, thanks [@​soryy708])

  • [Docs] order: Add a quick note on how unbound imports and --fix (#2640, thanks [@​minervabot])

title: (fix) Fix runtime (RT) tests and split tests in 2 actions (openhands/root)
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Fix mount issues for runtime (RT) tests. Split runtime unit tests for diff users.

---

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- `RuntimeClient` class (client): in `_init_user` the initial (mounted) folder now gets the right permissions set (g+rws)
- `Dockerfile.j2` template: added `openhands/workspace` folder with right permissions which can be used for mounting e.g. for unit test sub-folders etc.


- Split runtime (RT) unit tests into 2: one for root, one for openhands
- Tests that use a runtime will now get their own folder mounted in both host and sandbox to prevent clashes across tests
- Improved avoidance of port collisions with Docker by checking both host AND docker that a port is not in use
- Runtime will use port range 30000-39999, Jupyter Kernel 40000-49999 (tbd)
- The port is now also passed as an env variable into the sandbox (in addition to the url)

- In the 'conftest.py' the overall handling of folders has been rewritten and most tests adapted and tested with up to 3 concurrent core test runs
- Shortened runtime (RT) job names to better fit GitHub workflow window
- Added support for env var SKIP_CONTAINER_LOGS (bool, default false) to disable the extra logging of the last 1000 container log lines, which even in debug mode is more spam than not
- in `ghcr_runtime.yml` reduced `--reruns` to 1 (from 2) and added `--reruns-delay 3` so a rerun first waits 3 seconds. More reruns usually do not help in case of errors.

All in all, after many headaches at least with my WSL, more runtime tests are now successful, like the full 19 tests in `test_bash.py` ran through. Waiting for all tests now to finish...

In my WSL the test folders will be set like this (the runtime's sid will also be 26219 in this case):
Edit: below is outdated but the overall idea hasn't changed.
```
workspace_base: /mnt/d/github/workspace
workspace_mount_path: /mnt/d/github/workspace/test/26219
workspace_mount_path_in_sandbox: /openhands/workspace/test/26219
```
After each test finishes, its test folder will be removed again:
```
Removing test directory: /mnt/d/github/workspace/test/51582
Removed.
PASSED
```

---

**Link of any specific issues this addresses**
author: tobitege

title: Ketan simplified co act workflow
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

* This PR implements a simplified multi-agent workflow inspired by the [CoAct paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13381).
* Currently, in swe-bench eval, there are complex instances that OpenHands fails, especially ones that single CodeActAgent overlooks the buggy location. If we have a grounding test case for the issue, this workflow seems to help.
* An overkill-ish successful trajectory with replanning can be found [here](https://www.all-hands.dev/share?share_id=5d279ec840834fb326c8f3a2fcfc108bcbb27e4793c6a329e6515fa301c448ac).
* A task which CoActPlannerAgent finished but CodeActAgent failed (I expected both to be able to complete it):
[CoAct traj](https://www.all-hands.dev/share?share_id=197cb024a7eee24c8373b3ac1bbc5e905d274bbe0a869c3c4b7705158bcf4de6)
[CodeAct traj](https://www.all-hands.dev/share?share_id=6be13d7296b6bdfefdfc6e6a3a21e21198716a2ecd4494dd4962787f5105abe7)


---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
* Modify CodeAct to make it accept delegated task.
* Implement 2 new agents, planner and executor with the same abilities as CodeAct, different system prompts, additional action parsers.


---
**Link of any specific issues this addresses**

* Don't show the agent as loaded until the runtime is ready

* Filter files based on gitignore at the API level, not the runtime level
  * Runtime should have access to *all* files

Most controversial thing here is probably running `wait_until_alive` in the runtime constructor.

title: Refactor history/event stream
body:
**CHANGELOG**
Arch refactoring: 
- move most event filtering to the event stream
- refactor how agents and agent helpers like prompt templates work with the event history
- remove the ShortTermHistory class and move all its methods to the event stream or controller, as appropriate.

---

Tested with UI and `main.py`; new/old/restored sessions; delegates restore.

Note: I put the filtering delegates in the controller, although it could have been on the stream too. I don't know, I don't have a strong opinion about it, just it seems like adding dependencies on delegate events to the stream is a bit too detailed, and really the reason why delegates are filtered is very agent-related.

Fixes #3731 

---

To run this PR locally, use the following command:
```
docker run -it --rm   -p 3000:3000   -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock   --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway   -e SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/all-hands-ai/runtime:2732293-nikolaik   --name openhands-app-2732293   ghcr.io/all-hands-ai/runtime:2732293

title: Revert "chore(deps): bump numpy from 1.26.4 to 2.1.1"
body:
Reverts All-Hands-AI/OpenHands#3713

PR 3713 updated numpy from under 2.0.0 version to 2.1, and the solution dependabot found:
- downgraded a lot of other packages
- gives an error with chromadb we saw on python 3.12
- we also see the same error on [python 3.11](https://openhands-ai.slack.com/archives/C06U8UTKSAD/p1726038317702519)

I think we should revert. I am not sure why only some of us see this error and CI appears to work, but it looks like we can't update until llama/chroma do.

title: Refactor messages serialization
body:
**CHANGELOG**
Refactor the serialization of messages for vision, prompt caching, Groq incompatibilities.
- fix potential bug with shared list
- refactor the formatting we need to do into the serialization methods on the Message classes

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**
Groq documents on their site that their API is openai-compatible, and lists only a few limitations that don't affect us. Sadly, that's not quite right: for vision format, their API gives 400 errors because it requires both `system` and `assistant` message to be simple strings (as opposed to accepting lists of text/image content). Cc: @tobitege I had a wild hope that it is only the system message, but the fact that assistant message is also not supported makes it impossible to merge implementations completely for now...

It's possible that the vision models are too new still, and Groq and/or liteLLM haven't got yet to adapt to all changes. I'll follow up on that... In the meantime we have a potential bug in the Message class and I took the opportunity to synchronize the two implementations (vision and non-vision) we have.

Tested with: Groq/Llama 3.1 70B, Gemini 1.5 Flash (AI Studio), o1, Sonnet 3.5

Part of https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/issues/3812

title: [eval] yet another eval fixes on multi-processing
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

In https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/pull/3846, we introduce the ability to add a failed instance back to the `instance_queue` for future retry. But the original implementation has a bug: when running for a while, it will stuck there forever. I investigated the reason, it seems it is blocked by `queue.get()`.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- This PR (hopefully) fixes the multi-processing logic so that the `executor.submit` loop continues to run whenever (1) the instance queue is not empty OR (2) there's an unfinished process (future) running (bc it may add a new instance to the queue).
- nit: Increased timeout for `/swe_util/instance_swe_entry.sh` bc i found there's issue with 600 sec timeout in some cases.

title: [eval] refactor process instance logic into `update_progress`
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

The fixes in https://github.com/All-Hands-AI/OpenHands/pull/3854 fix most multi-processing issue, but at some point, we'd get errors like:

```
ERROR:asyncio:Task exception was never retrieved
future: <Task finished name='Task-109' coro=<Runtime.on_event() done, defined at /home/xingyaow/OpenDevin-dev/openhands/runtime/runtime.py:111> exception=HTTPError('404 Client Error: Not Found for url: https://21ca5bc7-c846-49b5-a77a-1287ad5d6069.runti
me.all-hands.dev/alive')>
```

Because we never directly called `future.result()` which cause asyncio to complain - this gets evaluation to stuck.

See relevant info [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/46890646/asyncio-weirdness-of-task-exception-was-never-retrieved).

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

This PR tries to fix this by:
- (1) refactoring all the exception handling into `update_progress` function, and get rid of the previous `process_instance` wrapper.
- (2) always call `future.results()` inside `update_progress` and handle exception from there



---

body:
**CHANGELOG**

This PR proposes a quick fix for eval trajectories missing delegate events.

---
**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

Please note: this PR can be reviewed. But it should not be merged yet, I need some testing.

Eval trajectories are computed by a compatibility method that uses the same source of events as the regular agent running, and that excludes events from the delegate agents that may have run during the task. This PR adds these events, if we want a quick fix.

title: Tightened up the logic on retries.
body: ## Requests retry for a very long time when an endoint fails: * 15 retries with an exponential backoff starting at 4 seconds and ending at 60 seconds == almost 10 minutes. * This does not include any time the http requests take to run - and these can have a timeout of a few minutes by default depending on the type of error involved. (So the actualy lock up can be way higher than 10 minutes) ## The Changes This changes the number of retries to a set time period of 2 minutes. (If the request does not succeed in 2 minutes, the user has probably long since lost interest and tried to cancel it.) ## Speaking of which... This is not handled by this PR, but the timeout actually locks up the server. For example: Here is output of me trying to `cmd+c` the server at 11:37:16... But the server did not actually die until 11:39:20 I will am working on a subsequent PR to address the lock up, but in the meantime I figure a lock up of 2 minutes is better than a lock up of 10+ minutes.

title: (enh) AgentSkills: fix \n handling with file editing (iPython)
body:
**Short description of the problem this fixes or functionality that this introduces. This may be used for the CHANGELOG**

Fixed handling of literal "\n" in file editing operations via iPython.

---

**Give a summary of what the PR does, explaining any non-trivial design decisions**

- in `file_ops.py` and `CodeActAgent.py` fixed handling of literal line breaks
- helps fix errors when LLM calls `edit_file_by_replace` but errors with `[No exact match found in xxx]`
